title: Optimization Relation Verdicts
description: relations.json (design spec 5.5): per-relation verdicts from the native property-test run, with the target-native test identifier and its exit status. Written by orchestrator.optimize.artifacts.write_relations from a list of orchestrator.optimize.relations.RelationVerdict. A relation declared but never executed (native_test not found in the target's results) is recorded as passed=false -- a typo'd identifier must never silently disable a correctness gate.

verdicts.description: One entry per declared (factor, relation) pair, in factor-then-relation declaration order.

correctness_failures.description: relation_ids of failed kind=correctness verdicts. Non-empty here means the campaign must hard-fail (design spec 6.4): the apparatus is broken and measurements are meaningless.

behavioral_failures.description: relation_ids of failed kind=behavioral verdicts. These are recorded findings, never a hard-fail -- a monotonicity violation is a discovery (e.g. the L5 batching sign-flip), not a bug.

relation_id.description: The relation's declared id, from factor.relations[].id.

factor_id.description: The factor this relation was declared on.

kind.description: correctness relations hard-fail the campaign when broken (conservation laws, no-op-at-baseline). behavioral relations (monotonicity) become findings and never fail the campaign.

native_test.description: Target-native property-test identifier (a pytest nodeid, a JUnit classname.name, etc.) that this relation delegates to. Nous never generates or interprets this test's code -- it only checks that this identifier ran and passed.

passed.description: False both for a test that ran and failed, and for a declared native_test that never appears in the results at all (declared-but-not-executed is a failure, never a silent pass).

detail.description: Human-readable detail: "passed", "native_test '...' failed", or "...declared native_test '...' but it was not executed...".
